record_notes.DCP-LETT-1769: October 25, supplied 1855. Four blocks, seven footnotes and bibliography read. Cannot provide information about Mrs Shaw; directory identification of John Shaw is editorial conjecture, not established relationship. Eyton dog work and pigs known, proposed museum visit future. Entomological recollections do not date a new specimen acquisition. No surviving current incoming note supplies a complete prompt.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1784: November 26, supplied 1855. Four blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. Darwin asks practical skeleton preparation questions after his own nauseating attempts; drying and boiling alternative is reported advice, not a completed successful procedure. Ten pairs of varieties alive now, two or three further kinds expected Saturday. Later 1856 outsourcing and recipe in apparatus are not current body content. This outgoing inquiry does not require an invented missing initiating Eyton letter.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1789: December 3, supplied 1855. Five blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. Missing advice thanked, pigeons in water and many alive; global collection remains intention. Chinese dog head only almost certainly owned and offered conditional on finding it. Spitz dog alive and young; possible eventual carcass gift is not a delivered specimen. No source-complete incoming advice in preserved catalogue.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1793: December 9, supplied 1855. Five blocks, seven footnotes and bibliography. Dog head not found; possible British Museum transfer explicitly unremembered and not proved. Intended Eyton gift about twelve years earlier, renewed contact at Glasgow. Nestlings in brine, work underway. Eyton skeleton loan offer known but Darwin not ready to profit from it, no physical receipt established. Several-year publication forecast distinct from later Eyton works and Variation. Yarrell breastbones shown, Tegetmeier skull series already given but paper prospective.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1525: July 24, supplied 1853, Eastbourne. Seven blocks, six footnotes and bibliography. Narrative finished last night, July 23 under supplied year; notebook entry dated July 20 is a different record/stage and not substituted for explicit completion. Unsolicited admiration renews acquaintance; future plans asked, family recollections and current sea-bathing. No preserved incoming Galton text needed to explain this initiative.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1881: May 28, editorially most likely 1854 despite a single supplied XML year. Eight blocks, three footnotes and bibliography. Direct FitzRoy quotation in P1 is not original Darwin observation; P2 personally saw pyrites objects, P3 mine apparatus report source forgotten, P4 Mullein vague hearsay, P5 Hibiscus recollection. P6 water-bird down trial suggested, not performed result. Galton later book does not include this particular information even though a different Darwin Falklands observation is used. Historical colonial wording retained as source attribution, not endorsed. Exact-year hold.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1627: January 1, supplied 1855. Three blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. Art of travel gift received yesterday, December 31, 1854, notwithstanding nominal 1855 title year; publication window consistent but not source of exact receipt. From what I have seen establishes selected inspection, not completion of entire book. London house search future. Apparatus 27 York Place versus 1631 body 28 York Place remains an unresolved address discrepancy, not silently harmonized.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1554F: February 22, supplied 1855. Three complete blocks, three footnotes and bibliography. Photocopy of four-page ALS, not a fragment simply because ID ends F. Galton note on pigeons acknowledged and Andersson offer obtained, actual African animal observations not yet delivered. Darwin asks Galton to forward this present note to Andersson, not to forward the offer. Questions about breeding, selection and famine remain questions, not established local practices. Supplied year assessed against cited 1854 response and residence chronology; no complete Galton prompt preserved.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1430: June 2, supplied 1851. Two blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. Metadata ALS two pages, earlier edition used copy. Gould April 9 note and Californian cirripede box both received yesterday, June 1 through Cuming. Fossil Lepadidae described as published, copy sending future; later full presentation-copy availability in September is a distinct production/distribution event. Recent volume about to go to press, half sessile work complete, loan returns prospective. Incoming April 9 body absent.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1475: February 29, supplied 1852. Four blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. Fossil copy already sent with Agassiz packet, delivery not confirmed. Recent volume copy deliberately not sent because Darwin believes Gould a Ray member and anticipates society distribution. End-of-year completion a forecast, not actual 1854 date. Ibla findings based on earlier specimens. Statement no answer required is historical content, not an agent instruction.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1591: September 9, supplied 1854. Five blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. Work finished and specimens packed; box via Williams and Norgate planned next week, no established dispatch or Gould arrival that day. Includes Agassiz specimens and copy, excludes Gould own copy on membership assumption. P3 all returned safely is qualified authorial belief within future-shipping context, not proof of actual receipt. Tetraclita stolen from parcel, duplicate exists, thief not identified. Prior Ibla dissection recalled.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1724: July 21, 1855. Four blocks, two footnotes and bibliography. Missing Lyell note received a few days since reports Gould approval, not a direct Gould letter. Possibly same communication as July 19 in 1720 but no evidence establishes identity, so no merged prompt or exact receipt. Two reserved copies offered if Gould no longer member; silence would be interpreted as membership, not proof a reply occurred. General distribution delayed after presentation copies; publication, allocation, sending and receipt distinct.

record_notes.DCP-LETT-1200: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. September 3, supplied 1848, September 5 postmark. record_notes.DCP-LETT-1251: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. August 20, supplied and postmarked 1849. Gould April 30 note and loan through Cuming reached Darwin only about a fortnight ago after absence; approximate interval, not exact August 6 arrival. Sessile specimens for future work; disarticulation permission sought with chance to object, not all already examined. Tavoy Ibla comparison contemporary. Quoted Gould offer in P4 is a short embedded fragment, not full incoming letter; drawing colour marks seen but whole drawings absent here. Scutella forwarding prospective, Dana letter already written, Conrad answer still absent. Editorial summary incorrectly thanks Dana; body clearly thanks Gould. Final published classifications separate.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1320: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. April 8, supplied 1850 from scientific/itinerary context. Found delayed Gould parcel yesterday at Cuming, where servant had put it aside during illness; earlier delivery there differs from Darwin access. Coronula promised by missing note was not enclosed; only large Balanus present. Dana hope of Scalpellum holdings reported, no incoming Dana text. Previous Darwin reminder missing. Yesterday would be April 7 under assigned year; April 10 meeting cited in apparatus is contextual, not identical visit day established.

record_notes.DCP-LETT-1631: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. Monday 15, supplied January 1855 ALS. Four blocks and two footnotes. Lubbock note received January 14; Darwin visited Baugh after breakfast January 15. Baugh now says case already laid before Commissioners, contrary to earlier threatened stage. Further Court of Equity and local law-cost subscription conditional; lawyer opinion reported through Baugh, not court judgment. Archbishop not discussed explicitly. London house taken, Thursday move and scientific meetings future, later itinerary not proof current attendance.
record_notes.DCP-LETT-1720: Explicit accepted primary full-source reading reused after matching note, ledger and source hashes. 19, supplied July 1855 ALS. Five blocks, four footnotes and bibliography. Missing Lyell note received this morning reports fossil Ovibos discovery, not direct Lubbock incoming. Darwin geological interpretation contemporary; 1856 Owen description and later publications excluded from current knowledge. June 16 Lyell-to-Lubbock letter cited in apparatus is a distinct correspondence witness, not this missing July 19-arrived Lyell note. P4 confirms Lubbock missed Tuesday invitation, contrasting earlier plan 1831.

reading_method: Root independently read complete surviving new source bodies, metadata constraints, exclusions, footnotes, scholarly sections and bibliography. Actual special markup and figures inspected where present. Reused explicit accepted primary readings only after matching source and accepted evidence hashes. Historical decisions and notes are handwritten; validation packages evidence rather than adjudicating it.
